allowed_implementation_freedom: Internal language types, module boundaries, algorithms, and storage are unconstrained when every cited observable distinction is preserved.
Exact diagnostic wording and ordering are unconstrained unless a cited authority explicitly requires them.
canonical_input_forms: exact Git worktree history, current profile, current working tree
non_normative_behaviors: Python object types, exception classes, module layout, and incidental algorithms are not semantic authority.
Rust crate, module, and internal type layout are not semantic authority.
required_state_distinctions: direct first accepted creation establishes a body seal and is valid
proposed body changes before acceptance are allowed
a changed body after acceptance is rejected
a published rewrite followed by restoration remains rejected
a current uncommitted rewrite is rejected
a first working-tree acceptance without historical anchor is allowed
accepted to superseded with identical body is accepted
accepted to superseded with changed body is rejected
first structured superseded state without prior acceptance does not seal
slug rename preserving logical ID and exact body is accepted
slug rename changing accepted body is rejected
a postacceptance matching symlink state is rejected
a postacceptance unstructured matching state is rejected
Git replace refs are ignored during historical inspection
a same-ID impostor outside the canonical corpus is ignored
an unrelated non-UTF8 path outside the ADR directory is ignored
a nested non-UTF8 path under the ADR directory is ignored
a direct non-UTF8 child cannot enter the textual filename-pattern domain and is ignored
a non-UTF8 path under an ADR-directory prefix collision is ignored
